Because the required document could not be accessed with the browsing tools available, I cannot provide a definitive list. If you have access to the RAP Bulletin 73 or to a supplementary material file (often hosted by Conservation International or on the CI website), reviewing the bat section of that report would give the precise list of Phyllostominae species documented at Alto Mayo in 2022.

The RAP program’s official report (RAP Bulletin 73) was the primary source that would contain this information, but I could not retrieve the full PDF or a detailed chapter on bats. Other public-facing news releases and summary articles about the Alto Mayo expedition mention that a handful of bat species were observed, but they do not provide an explicit, taxonomic checklist of Phyllostomidae or of the specific sub‑family Phyllostominae.

Because the required document could not be accessed with the browsing tools available, I cannot provide a definitive list. If you have access to the RAP Bulletin 73 or to a supplementary material file (often hosted by Conservation International or on the CI website), reviewing the bat section of that report would give the precise list of Phyllostominae species documented at Alto Mayo in 2022.
